summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change the terminology used for financial product information that does not consider a consumer's personal circumstances, replacing general advice with general information.
It would require warnings to retail clients to say the information is not advice, alongside the existing warning that personal objectives, finances and needs are unconsidered.
The terminology and warning amendments would begin the day after six months from royal assent, giving providers time before the substantive requirements would apply.
changes: References to general advice across the Corporations Act would be replaced with general information.
The client warning in section 949A would expressly distinguish general information from advice.
The preliminary provisions would begin on the day after royal assent.
summary.affected: Financial product information providers, financial advisers and retail clients receiving general information are affected.
